heuristic.applicability: Prefer when the high-level agent has a reliable current drawer anchor pose and drawer_position, and the drawer is closed, partly open, or being pulled with the TCP plausibly near the front. It is especially relevant when the cabinet anchor differs from training or the policy is entered after some opening progress. The supplied anchor must describe the same articulated drawer convention as training.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer closed or partly open with a reliable anchor and drawer_position; TCP high/free or plausibly at the front; gripper state observable; red supported in the drawer and blue outside. Reachability remains a high-level responsibility.
handoff.exit_conditions: Nominal exit is drawer_position safely above the unchanged strict 0.26-m task threshold, drawer velocity near zero, front contact released, and observable red/TCP co-motion after closure and initial lift. A closed gripper alone is not proof of grasp.
handoff.failure_signatures: Drawer remains at or below 0.26, drawer moves without matching TCP/front geometry, anchor estimate jumps, fingers drag or miss the front, red/TCP XY remain misaligned on descent, fingers close without red co-motion, IK is unconverged, or red drops during lift.
handoff.overlap_role: Retains all actions 0:470. The 230:470 portion in every one of 12 trajectories is action-supervised overlap with red_transfer: front release, retreat, red approach/descent, closure and initial lift (240 actions per occurrence, 2,880 total).
handoff.successor_readiness: red_transfer may receive once drawer_position is above 0.26 and red is exposed; nominal readiness is stronger when fingers are closed and red/TCP co-motion is observed by about 470. The overlap supports switches before or after release/contact.

heuristic.limitations: Rigid frame equivariance does not establish a grasp or recover a missed front. Large shifts/rotations can be unreachable or collide, and only one drawer orientation and one approximately 0.300-m terminal opening are demonstrated. The post-opening red pickup is represented relative to the drawer but is not invariant by construction to independent red displacement within the drawer; observed red variation is only about x 0.093-0.108 and y -0.077 to -0.055 before opening. Fresh-frame decoding can also propagate a bad drawer pose estimate. The alternative tcp_increment_servo is less sensitive to anchor error for local motion, while phase_conditioned_world targets stage ambiguity at nominal calibration. Successful demonstrations do not prove unseen-error recovery.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: The caller supplies drawer_origin_world_m, drawer_orientation_wxyz, and desired_open_position_m. The executor still supplies fresh drawer_position and measured joints. Use this policy for displaced drawer geometry or partial-opening entries. For a nominal cabinet but a perturbed TCP or tracking lag, prefer tcp_increment_servo; for an uncertain nominal phase with reliable world calibration, phase_conditioned_world is the complementary choice. The standard Diffusion Policy backbone is retained because the needed invariant is implemented in input/target/decode coordinates, not by changing temporal modeling.
heuristic.rationale: Observed evidence: in demo1000 the TCP settles near the closed drawer front by 140, the fingers are closed and drawer_position is 0.0106 at 160, and TCP, red, and drawer then translate together mainly along world -X until drawer_position reaches 0.300 by 220-230. The TCP remains at the open front through release at 240 and retreats upward by 280-300. Demo1001 shows the same relation while red Y differs. The demonstrations have a single cabinet anchor and nearly identical approach/pull timing, so memorized world targets are a likely failure if the drawer anchor or entry opening differs. The policy will express every commanded Cartesian pose as position plus 6D rotation in the currently observed drawer frame. That frame is formed from the caller-supplied drawer origin/orientation and translated by the fresh drawer_position along drawer local -X for every label and every decoded action. This makes the approach, front acquisition, pull tracking, release, and initial retreat equivariant by construction to a supplied rigid drawer-anchor displacement and reactive to intermediate drawer opening. Robot qpos/qvel, TCP-to-drawer, red-to-drawer, drawer velocity and desired opening remain inputs, preserving reachability, articulation and contact-relevant dependencies. No synthetic augmentation is used; demonstrated commanded TCP poses remain physically valid labels. Expected benefit, not observed success: less world-position extrapolation for reachable shifted/partially open drawers.
heuristic.statement: Drawer-frame Cartesian tracking for displaced or partially open drawers

assignment.subgoal: Primary responsibility: acquire the drawer front, pull the drawer from closed to a reliably open state, release/retract from the drawer, and continue through the demonstrated handoff until the red block is grasped and beginning to lift. Observed contact/motion: the gripper approaches low over the drawer front, closes, pulls mainly along world -X, then opens and retreats upward before moving above and descending to the exposed red block; gripper/object co-motion is used only as an observable contact cue because contact truth is unavailable. Entry is a closed drawer (drawer_position about 0), open gripper, high TCP, red inside the drawer, and blue outside. At the nominal exit observation 470, drawer_position is 0.300, fingers are about 0.018 m, and red is grasped and lifted to z about 0.093-0.107 m while blue is unchanged. Examples: demo1000 observations 230/280 show the fully opened drawer followed by release/vertical retreat; 400/445/470 show red alignment, closure, and lift. The front images at demo1000 indices 150, 230, and 445 support the drawer-pull, open-drawer, and red-contact interpretation. Purpose/expected benefit: the retained post-opening transition should let the red-transfer successor accept a switch before or after drawer release and red contact; it is not evidence of recovery from unseen failed pulls or misgrasps.

check.checkpoint_selection: last EMA at the declared update budget

conversion_check.description: For valid labels, drawer-frame encode/decode reconstructs the demonstrated commanded world TCP pose; shared IK is checked by FK position/rotation and the unchanged gripper scalar. Gram-Schmidt only projects sampled non-orthogonal 6D rotations.

contract.cut_relation: Covers every assigned action in each [0,470) segment. It retains approach, front acquisition, pull, release, retreat, red approach/closure and initial lift, including the full action-supervised 230:470 overlap with red_transfer.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is an absolute TCP target expressed in the drawer frame computed at that slot's pre-action observation: relative position [3] in metres, relative rotation as the first two rotation-matrix columns [6], then native gripper scalar [1]. At execution, slots 1..8 correspond to current t..t+7. Every slot is transformed through the drawer frame recomputed from the fresh current drawer_position and caller calibration. Rotation 6D is projected by Gram-Schmidt, then the world target is passed to panda_kinematics.solve_ik from freshly measured qpos. The gripper scalar is appended unchanged and the common executor maps its sign to open/close.
contract.parameter_semantics: drawer_origin_world_m is the current world-frame origin in metres of the drawer at drawer_position=0. drawer_orientation_wxyz is its unit wxyz orientation and defines local -X opening translation. desired_open_position_m is the intended scalar opening in metres, bound to the demonstrated 0.300 m. Fresh drawer_position and measured robot/object state come from the executor.
